strengths: Clear and well-motivated contribution: Identifies genuine limitations of existing AR models (order constraints, training inefficiency, attention redundancy) and proposes a principled solution through decoupled two-pass decoding
Strong empirical results: Achieves FID 1.83 on ImageNet-1K with 32 steps (30× speedup vs. LlamaDen), 75% memory reduction vs. VAR, while maintaining or improving generation quality

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Thorough ablations, multiple generation tasks (class-conditional, text-to-image, controllable, zero-shot), attention visualization, and scalability analysis across model sizes
Excellent reproducibility: Detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, architecture specifications, theoretical proof in appendices, and PyTorch pseudo-code provided
Technically sound: Correct mathematical formulation, well-justified two-pass architecture, valid theoretical analysis of masked modeling inefficiency in Appendix C
Strong presentation: Well-organized paper with effective visualizations and logical progression from motivation through methodology to experiments
Versatile applicability: Successfully demonstrated across diverse generation tasks (controllable generation, inpainting, editing, zero-shot inference) indicating robust generalization
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: The two-pass decoder concept is relatively straightforward given the problem; decoupling queries to attend KV cache is an incremental architectural modification

Incomplete comparative analysis: Comparisons with different model sizes/training data, missing some recent parallel decoding methods, and the claimed 30× speedup is specific to LlamaDen comparison; speedup varies across baselines
Insufficient evaluation metrics: Relies primarily on FID/IS without perceptual metrics or human evaluation; text-to-image evaluation is limited with few baselines
Limited exploration of design choices: RoPE justification is weak, ablation on position encoding impact is missing, KV cache interaction with random ordering needs deeper explanation
Training efficiency underanalyzed: Inference efficiency is well-documented but training cost comparisons are limited; no detailed wall-clock training time comparisons
Narrow experimental scope: Evaluation primarily on natural images (ImageNet, BLIP-3o); limited exploration on artistic/sketch domains or high-resolution images
Insufficient practical analysis: Memory reduction claimed but not deeply analyzed; no discussion of hardware requirements, deployment considerations, or failure cases
